answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using trust-network flow bounds. Participants issue bilateral credit lines, channeling a steady river of verified transactions. When an adversary deploys an island of cloned identities, their influence is bottlenecked by the sparse bridge edges linking to honest nodes. This forces attackers to stake scarce capital per gateway rather than creating costless agents. However, honest newcomers face high friction before securing trusted peers.
